summary: The bill creates a federal paid family and medical leave insurance program run by the Social Security Administration that pays eligible workers a percentage of their average monthly earnings (subject to minimum and maximum amounts) for up to 12 weeks of leave per year to care for themselves or family members with serious health conditions, bond with a new child, or address needs arising from domestic violence or similar acts.

scores.thoughts: The bill creates a new federal paid family and medical leave insurance program administered by the Social Security Administration, including benefit payments, a new Deputy Commissioner office, administrative infrastructure, grants to legacy states, and ongoing reporting requirements. This represents a major expansion of federal expenditures on a new entitlement-style benefit program.
The bill text contains no provisions that raise, lower, or otherwise modify taxes. While it is referred to the Ways and Means Committee, the legislation itself does not address revenue measures.
The bill provides paid leave for serious health conditions but does not alter health insurance coverage, public programs, or market-based healthcare structures. Any connection is incidental.
The bill has no provisions related to firearms, gun regulations, or gun rights.
The bill has no provisions related to immigration pathways, border enforcement, or immigrant protections.
The bill has no provisions addressing abortion access or restrictions.
The bill has no provisions related to military or defense spending.
The bill has no provisions related to environmental protections or regulations.

The bill establishes a new federal paid leave benefit program modeled on Social Security-style insurance, directly expanding the social safety net to cover family and medical caregiving needs for eligible workers.
The bill has no provisions related to schools, school choice, or federal education policy.
The bill has no provisions related to drug enforcement, decriminalization, or substance policy.
The bill has no provisions related to sentencing, policing, or criminal justice reform.
The bill has no provisions related to trade, tariffs, or globalization.

By creating a new spending program without identified offsetting revenue in the text, the bill implicitly accepts additional deficit spending, but this is secondary to its primary focus on establishing benefits.

The bill explicitly includes broad definitions of 'qualified family member' and 'domestic partner' that encompass same-sex relationships, civil unions, and relationships 'equivalent of a family relationship,' thereby extending benefits to LGBTQ+ individuals and families.
The bill has no provisions related to foreign aid.
The bill has no provisions related to voting access or election integrity.
The bill has no provisions related to technology regulation or data privacy.

The bill mandates job restoration, maintenance of health benefits, anti-retaliation protections, and enforcement mechanisms for workers taking leave, directly strengthening worker protections in employment.
The bill contains no provisions addressing religious exemptions or conflicts with anti-discrimination rules.
